newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan retail sales still dampened by tax increase.
newsitem.headline: Japan retail sales still dampened by tax increase.

text.p: Retail sales in Japan slumped again in June, hit by lingering aftershocks from a national sales tax increase in April that has made consumers cautious.

Sales at chain stores dropped 5.1 percent in June from a year ago to 1.33 trillion yen ($11.4 billion), while department store sales sagged 4.7 percent to 668.8 billion yen ($5.76 billion), industry groups announced on Thursday.

The Japan Chain Stores Association said that chain store sales fell for the third consecutive month in June on a year-on-year basis, although compared with May they were down a more modest 1.3 percent.
The association added that sales in the first half of 1997 fell 0.9 percent to 8.18 trillion yen ($70.5 billion) from the same period a year ago.

"Sales of home appliances (in June) were especially sluggish after consumers rushed to buy them before the rise in the consumption tax in April," said a spokesman for the group. The tax was raised to five percent from three percent on April 1.

The spokesman said a heat wave in late June that hit the Kanto region, Japan's economic centre which includes the two largest cities of Tokyo and Yokohama, boosted sales of summer products such as beer and air conditioners, but not enough to significantly change the overall sales figures.

Sales at Japanese department stores also slid on a year-on-year basis in June for the third month in a row, the Japan Department Stores' Association said. For the first half of the year, however, sales were up 0.4 percent from the year-ago period at 4.2 trillion yen ($36.2 billion).
In contrast to such gloom, convenience stores are posting solid sales growth.
Seven-Eleven Japan Co Ltd, the nation's largest convenience store chain operator, said on Thursday that sales growth had been firm thanks to the hot weather and robust demand for new products.
A company spokesman said that sales in June and July rose at a higher rate than the average 2.1 percent year-on-year growth rate recorded in the same months last year.
"The hot weather in the latter half of June helped boost sales of ice cream and soft drinks," he said.
